issues_confirmed: models/linear_regression.py:10 - logging.basicConfig(filename='test/LinearReg_debug.log') runs at import time; test/ is gitignored (.gitignore:27) and absent from disk, so 'import models' raises FileNotFoundError. models/__init__.py:4 imports this module, so every model is unreachable. Reproduced today; identical to the 2026-09-18 finding, never fixed.

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:40-55 - matrix_vector_multiply sizes vec_arr from len(vec) but vector_math.cpp:25 loops to cols=len(matrix[0]); a short vec causes an out-of-bounds read in C++. matrix_vector_multiply([[0,0,1],[0,0,2]], [0.0]) returned [8.3214395e-317, 1.6642879e-316] then [8.321439e-317, 1.6642878e-316] on the next call. Reachable from LinearRegression.predict / LogisticRegression.predict, neither of which checks X's column count against len(self.weights).

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:18-31,57-64 - dot/add/euclidean_distance set size=len(a) and then build b's buffer at that size, silently zero-padding a shorter b. euclidean_distance([3,4,99],[0,0]) returned 99.12618221237011. KNN.predict therefore answers dimension-mismatched queries with a confident label and no warning.

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:40-55 + models/linear_regression.py:41 + models/logistic_regression.py:25 - X is re-flattened and re-copied into a fresh c_double array on every call, inside the epoch loop, though X is constant across all epochs (1000 by default). Benchmarked at 2000x20, 20 reps: marshalling X alone 0.249s, full call 0.260s, pure-Python equivalent 0.129s, call with X pre-marshalled 0.001s. The C++ path is 2x slower than pure Python and 260x off its own ceiling.

models/knn.py:31 + README.md:41 - _predict_single crosses the ctypes boundary once per training row, re-marshalling the query vector each time. Benchmarked at 2000x20, 20 reps: 0.542s via CPP_vector.euclidean_distance vs 0.028s via stdlib math.dist (identical results) - 19x slower. README.md:41 claims distances are 'offloaded to C++ to handle larger datasets efficiently'; the opposite is true as written.

ml_math/utils.py:8 - sigmoid uses 1/(1+math.exp(-x)) and raises OverflowError: math range error for x <= about -710 (sigmoid(-700) = 9.85967654375977e-305, sigmoid(-710) raises). LogisticRegression.fit (logistic_regression.py:26) feeds w.x+b in unguarded.

ml_math/utils.py:10,48 - min_max_scaler and standard_scaler compute column statistics from the matrix passed in and discard them, so training scaling cannot be applied to held-out data. min_max_scaler([[0.0],[10.0]]) -> [[0.0],[1.0]] and min_max_scaler([[5.0],[20.0]]) -> [[0.0],[1.0]], where the test rows should map to 0.5 and 2.0 under the training scale. The arithmetic is correct; the API shape causes the error.

Makefile:21-25 + .gitignore:27 - 'make test' invokes five scripts under test/. git ls-files returns zero test files and the directory does not exist on disk, so the command the README tells users to run fails immediately. There are no tests in this repository.

models/linear_regression.py:25-29 - the TypeError fallback sets n_features=1 and prints a reassuring message, then crashes anyway at :41 because matrix_vector_multiply also calls len(matrix[0]). It converts a clear error into a misleading message followed by the same error.
models/linear_regression.py:38,45-47 - three logging.debug calls with eagerly-evaluated f-strings sit inside the per-sample loop, giving 3 * n_samples * 1000 formatted records at default settings.

docs/kaggle-learning-notes/main_question.md:80-83 - points at kaggle_titanic/, prediction_modeling/, and research_reports/run_logs/, none of which exist in this repo; wiki/INDEX.md:3 still names its origin repo (kaggle_strategies_models) and lists no pages.

verdict: Architecturally sound and genuinely interesting, but abandoned in place: six months since the last code commit, the package does not import, there are no tests, and the C++ backend that is the whole point is currently measurably slower than pure Python because every call re-marshals its inputs. Roughly two focused hours would make it work and make the C++ premise true - if nobody will spend them, this is not an active project and should be re-tiered.
